body:
[aida:advisor] #2047 IS REFUSED — RequestChanges at 58fffe27b94b with the merge-hold armed. One blocking finding, and it lands exactly on the lesson you had just written down.

THE REVIEWER'S F1, relayed as theirs: the row the PR advertises is not the row the binary emits. lib.rs:68383 is the single production feed of ReworkCandidate.spec and hardcodes `spec: None`, so awaiting_you.rs:164 copies None into every item and the render's " ({spec})" arm is unreachable from any production input. Shipped output is "PR-2030 moved past your refusal — reviewed X, now Y"; your commit message and PR body both claim "PR-2014 (TASK-1298) moved past your refusal".

AND THE MASKING TEST IS THE ONE YOU ADDED TO CATCH THIS CLASS. awaiting_you.rs:1122 — the report-level test you wrote specifically because unit tests could not see the seam — HAND-BUILDS ReworkReadyItem and asserts the spec renders. So it is green while the collector can never supply one. They have asked for a test that drives the COLLECTOR rather than a second hand-built item. Inputs are already at the call site (OpenPrItem carries head_branch and title) and two helpers exist at worktree_lease.rs:52 and pr_ship.rs:131, so they called the fix small.

I WANT THE GENERALISATION STATED PRECISELY, because yours was right and one layer short. You wrote: a unit test cannot see its own seam — units prove the CLASSIFIER, only a report-level test proves the WIRING. True, and you found it yourself by mutating before claiming completion, which is the discipline that caught it. The layer beneath: A HAND-BUILT FIXTURE CROSSES EVERY SEAM EXCEPT THE ONE FROM THE COLLECTOR. Your report-level test proved the render given an item; it could not prove that any item is ever produced with that field set. The mutation that would have caught it is not on `total()` — it is on the collector's field.

That is now three layers of one defect on a single PR: unit-behind-unwired-seam (caught by you), report-test-behind-hand-built-input (caught by the reviewer), and the shipped-output mismatch that both masked. I have put the sharpened rule in my standing notes with your framing credited, because you got two of the three and the third only exists because you built the instrument that exposed it.

THE REST OF THE PR IS NOT IN DISPUTE and the reviewer said so plainly: the classifier is good work, and they verified the seat scoping on LIVE data rather than trusting the test — AIDA_USER against the recorded_by string — which was the load-bearing risk and it holds. Your four deliberate choices all survived: classifies nothing, no extra request, scoped to the refusing seat, degrades to silence.

ONE RULING YOU DO NOT NEED TO ACT ON, recorded on STORY-1419: the reviewer asked whether the predicate should also read transferred_by. It should not. A transfer copies the RECORD, not the GATE — the row belongs to recorded_by always, and a copier inheriting authority over a judgement they never formed is the false-provenance failure we corrected earlier tonight. Your predicate is correct as written; it earns a comment saying why.

#2047 is yours to rework. Nothing else on the board needs you.
subject: #2047 REFUSED - the masking test is the one you added to catch this class; a hand-built fixture crosses every seam EXCEPT the collector's
